title: Our Eyes Are on the LORD

verses.text: I lift up my eyes to You, the One enthroned in heaven.
As the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master, as the eyes of a maidservant look to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes are on the LORD our God until He shows us mercy.
Have mercy on us, O LORD, have mercy, for we have endured much contempt.
We have endured much scorn from the arrogant, much contempt from the proud.

context.author: The title calls it “A song of ascents,” one of fifteen such psalms (120-134). They may have been sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the feasts; the Mishnah says the Levites sang them on the fifteen steps inside the Temple courts (Sukkah 5:4).
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.setting: “I lift up my eyes to You, the One enthroned in heaven” (v.1). The pilgrims watch God the way servants watch their master: “As the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master, as the eyes of a maidservant look to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes are on the LORD our God until He shows us mercy” (v.2). They are worn down: “Have mercy on us, O LORD, have mercy, for we have endured much contempt. We have endured much scorn from the arrogant, much contempt from the proud” (vv.3-4).
context.custom: Servants in a household waited silently for their master’s or mistress’s signal, a small motion of the hand, to know what to do. The scorn of v.4 fits the years after the exile, when neighbors mocked the returned Jews as they rebuilt Jerusalem (Nehemiah 2:19; 4:1-4).
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 124: “If the LORD had not been on our side.”
context.timelineBible: Hebrews says, “Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith” (Hebrews 12:2). The blind men cried, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!” (Matthew 20:30).

translation.meaning: Eye; also a spring of water.

gospelParallels.note: Insulted for the name of Christ.

otBackground.note: I lift up my eyes to the hills.

overview.summary: Scorned by the proud, God’s people lift their eyes to Him and watch Him as servants watch their master’s hand, waiting until He shows mercy.

archaeology.t: Egyptian tomb models show servants at work for their masters.
Excavations show a small city after the return from exile.

overview.discussion: Servants watch their master’s hand for the smallest signal (v.2). How closely am I watching for God’s direction?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: Not named
